sectionTitle: What changed beyond the sales office

primary.headline: Why Buying a New Home Is Now Cheaper Than an Existing One in Many Markets
primary.summary: Reporting cites recent market data showing the long-standing new-construction price premium over resale homes has narrowed or inverted in a number of U.S. metros, driven by builders' sustained use of rate buydowns, price cuts, and closing-cost credits to move inventory -- the same mechanism this sweep tracks daily in Austin. The piece frames this as a structural shift in buyer leverage rather than a one-off sale.
primary.buyerImplication: Directly validates what this sweep's own data has shown for months: Austin-area builders are carrying median advertised incentives around $25,000-$30,000 across 30+ active builders, with several offers exceeding $80,000-$105,000 on specific communities. Buyers comparing a new build to a comparable resale listing should run the full cost comparison (price, incentive value, HOA, warranty, and lender-tied rate terms) rather than assuming resale is cheaper by default.
primary.buyerAction: Before ruling out new construction as the pricier option, get the builder's current incentive-adjusted price in writing and compare it against a comparable resale listing's true closing cost -- not just list price. Use this sweep's Biggest Live Dollar Offers table as a starting point for which Austin-area builders are currently most aggressive.
primary.confidence: High confidence -- FOX 7 Austin reporting, published 2026-10-04; re-verified 2026-10-10 (7th consecutive day in rotation) after a fresh search pass found no fresher qualifying Austin/corridor story (the only new corridor hit was a 2023 Community Impact piece, checked and rejected on recency). Recency score stepped down as the story ages; total 78 remains above the 70-point publish bar. Market figures are as characterized in the source reporting.
